strings.name: Juan Manuel Santos
strings.role: Former Colombian president · Nobel Peace laureate
strings.summary: A journalist and economic-policy official before serving as minister, Santos was Colombia’s president in 2010–2018. He and negotiating teams advanced a government–FARC peace agreement, earning the 2016 Nobel Peace Prize, though not ending all armed violence. He apologized for the military’s killing of civilians presented as combat casualties during his defence ministry. Chair of The Elders since 2024, he continues peace and environmental advocacy.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: As Colombia’s president he advanced a peace agreement with an armed organization and received the Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to end prolonged conflict.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Peace agreement with FARC
strings.highlights.h1.text: Government and FARC negotiating teams reached a revised 2016 agreement after setbacks; the Nobel recognized his efforts.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Business and economics degrees, University of Kansas (1973); later postgraduate studies at LSE, Harvard and other institutions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Continuing public advocacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: After office, promoted peace, environment and multilateral cooperation; became Elders chair in 2024.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Chairs The Elders
strings.timeline.t1.text: Succeeded Mary Robinson, continuing work on peace and global public issues.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Apology over civilian killings
strings.timeline.t2.text: Apologized before the Truth Commission for military killings falsely presented as combat casualties during his defence ministry.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Presidency ends
strings.timeline.t3.text: Left after two terms and founded Compaz to support peacebuilding.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Revised peace agreement signed
strings.timeline.t4.text: Government and FARC signed a revised text; implementation still faces political and security challenges.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: Recognized for efforts to end prolonged civil war, not a claim that every conflict had ended.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes president
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began first term after ministerial and party leadership roles; reelected in 2014.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Defence minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served until 2009, directing operations against FARC as the military civilian-killing scandal emerged.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Kansas graduation
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed economics and business degrees before further postgraduate study.
